rows.source: LeCun & Balestriero, "Proving and Improving the Platonic Representation Hypothesis with JEPA" (29 Oct), via MindStudio's write-up
rows.claim: A learned world model that predicts in an abstract representation space rather than raw pixels or words, so it can ignore unpredictable detail; a ~109M-parameter JEPA model reportedly beat models up to 72B on one world-understanding benchmark
rows.evidence: One paper, one benchmark, read through a vendor blog
rows.done: Poesys's world is an explicit simulation built from the GB record, not a learned model, and must stay inspectable and fail-closed behind the wall. The one echo: model what matters at the level it is predictable (aggregate observables, not exact household detail) — already how the world is built.
